correctness.rationale: Each nonidentity output has a unique changed-support interval with length 2..k. Every endpoint-changing anagram of an interval is realizable by a containing length-k window since n>=k. Inclusion-exclusion for multinomial anagrams counts H(u) exactly. If a block repeats, H<=m!/2<c_m for m>=4, with direct m=2 and m=3 boundary checks; pairwise-distinct blocks attain c_m. Termwise strictness proves sharpness and iff rigidity, and q!/(q-k)! then q-k+1 choices at each extension give the exact population. Independent direct-output checks covered 12,176 words; finite tests are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The worst-case number of distinguishable outputs is a natural precise ambiguity invariant of the local permutation channel, including DNA-motivated q=k=4. The result gives a sharp closed formula, a full rigidity criterion and exact extremizer census simultaneously for arbitrary window lengths and input lengths, not a new decoder or code-size bound. These are substantive structural facts not mechanically implied by the accessible binary redundancy bounds or prior k=3 specialization.

final_claim: For all integers q>=k>=4 and n>=k, the maximum cardinality of the distinct outputs of exactly one non-wrapping length-k arbitrary-permutation burst is 1+sum_{m=2}^k (n-m+1)(m!-2(m-1)!+(m-2)!), with equality exactly when every length-k window of the input has pairwise distinct symbols, and with exactly q!/(q-k)!*(q-k+1)^(n-k) maximizing words.
limitations: Only q>=k>=4 and n>=k, exactly one non-wrapping arbitrary-permutation window; no q<k extremal optimization, multisets across multiple windows, multiple bursts, or coding-rate guarantees.
Finite checks validate bounded instances only; the infinite theorem rests on the support decomposition and strict multinomial inequalities.
